pages.title: Introduction & The Creation
pages.content:
Adam (pbuh) is the first Messenger and the father of all humans. Allah created him from soil and showed him great respect and gave him full value as the first human. The Holy Qur’an tells his tale in different surahs. Surahs A’raf, Baqarah, Hijr, Isra, Sad and Taha describe Adam (pbuh)’s tale clearly. As the grandchildren of Adam (pbuh), we can learn many lessons from this fabulous but true story. In this story, there are numerous important messages about humans’ role in life.

After Allah created the sky and the earth, He told the angels that He was going to create a human. He said He had decided to place a ruler (khalifah) on earth. This ruler would live there for many years. The angels were surprised and began to wait with curiosity.

vocabulary.definition: A person chosen by Allah to deliver His message.
Very impressive or wonderful.
A person given responsibility to lead or manage.
A strong wish to know more.

hotspots.title: Created from Soil
hotspots.description: Allah created Adam (pbuh) from soil and honored him as the first human.

hotspots.title: Responsibility on Earth
hotspots.description: Allah told the angels that He would place a ruler, or khalifa, on earth.

exercises.title: The Angels’ Reaction
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: Allah told the angels that He would place a ruler on earth. How did the angels react?
options: They thought they were better than the new human.
They were surprised and began to wait with curiosity.
They admired Adam and showed respect to him.
exercises.explanation: The last sentence of Chapter 1 says: “The angels were surprised and began to wait with curiosity.” Adam was not created yet, so the angels could not admire him at this point. That happens in Chapter 3, and the feeling of being “better” belongs to Iblis, not to the angels.

feedback.correct: Yes. The news surprised the angels, and they waited to see what would happen.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 1 again. Remember that Adam is not created yet in this chapter.

languageFocusExercises.title: True Now or Happened Then?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part of Chapter 1 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it true now, or did it happen in the story?

items: Adam (pbuh) is the first Messenger and the father of all humans.
The Holy Qur’an tells his tale in different surahs.
we can learn many lessons from this fabulous but true story
Allah created him from soil
… gave him full value as the first human.
The angels were surprised

True now (present forms): Adam (pbuh) is the first Messenger and the father of all humans.
The Holy Qur’an tells his tale in different surahs.
we can learn many lessons from this fabulous but true story
Happened in the story (past forms): … gave him full value as the first human.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The present simple (is, tells) and “can” describe things that are true today: Adam’s place as the first Messenger, what the Qur’an does, and what we can learn now. The past simple (created, gave, were) tells finished events inside the story. Even in the first paragraph, “Allah created him from soil” is past because it is an event, not a present fact.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated present facts about Adam, the Qur’an and us from past story events.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb in each part: is, tells, can learn, or created, gave, were? Then ask: Is this still true today, or did it happen once in the story?

languageFocusExercises.title: Order, Report, Look Forward
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 1 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word orders the events, which reports words, and which looks ahead?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank] Allah created the sky and the earth, He [blank] the angels that He was going to create a human. … This ruler [blank] live there for many years.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “After + past simple” puts one finished event before the next: First the sky and the earth, then the announcement. We “tell someone” something, but we “say something” (not “said the angels”). “Would” and “was going to” look forward from a past moment: When the angels were told, the ruler’s long life on earth was still in the future. “Will” looks forward from now, so it does not fit a story told in the past.

feedback.correct: Correct. You ordered the events, reported the announcement, and looked forward from the past.
feedback.incorrect: Check the second paragraph of Chapter 1. Which came first? Who was told? Is the ruler’s future seen from now or from that past moment?

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about Allah’s plan and the angels?

errorItems.sentence: He said He has decided to place a ruler (khalifah) on earth.
The angels were surprised and began wait with curiosity.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: When we report a decision after a past verb (He said …), a decision made before that moment moves back to the past perfect: “He said He had decided …”. After “began”, use “to + base verb” (or -ing): “began to wait”. “Began” is already past, so the verb after it does not change.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the past perfect and the pattern after “began”.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 1 again: “He said He … to place a ruler” and “The angels were surprised and began …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Connected Account
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about how the story of Adam (pbuh) begins.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you tell how the story begins?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can begin with a present source statement, shift into past narration, order events with “after”, and use “was going to” or “would” for future-from-the-past meaning.

feedback.correct: Keep the time perspective consistent and connect the ideas rather than writing four unrelated sentences.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Name the source: “The Qur’an tells …”
discussionPrompts.example: The Qur’an tells the story of Adam (pbuh) in different surahs, such as Surah Baqarah and Surah Taha.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Start the story: “After …, Allah …”
discussionPrompts.example: After Allah created the sky and the earth, He decided to create a human.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what He told the angels: “He told the angels that …”
discussionPrompts.example: He told the angels that He was going to place a ruler on earth.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what would happen later: “… was going to …” or “… would …”
discussionPrompts.example: This ruler would live on earth for many years, so the angels waited with curiosity.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What did Allah create Adam (pbuh) from?

iCan: I can say what Allah told the angels before He created Adam (pbuh).
I can say what someone was going to do later.
I can write four linked sentences about the start of a story.

pages.title: The Shaping of Adam
pages.content:
Then, Allah’s angels collected soil from different parts of the earth and Allah shaped Adam (pbuh). That’s why humans have different skin colors. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said that Allah created Adam (pbuh) from a handful of dust from different lands, so the children of Adam (pbuh) are white, red, black and yellow in color. 

Allah told His angels, “After I have created Adam (pbuh) and given him life and knowledge, show respect to him.” Allah gave Adam (pbuh) life and intellect to learn and understand. Later, He taught Adam (pbuh) everything he needed to do good on earth. He gave Adam (pbuh) more knowledge than the angels.

vocabulary.definition: An amount that can be held in one hand.
The ability to reason, learn, and understand.
Information and understanding that someone has.
Gave something a particular form.

hotspots.title: Soil from Many Lands
hotspots.description: The angels collected soil from different parts of the earth, so humans have different skin colors.

hotspots.title: A Gift of Knowledge
hotspots.description: Allah gave Adam (pbuh) life, intellect and more knowledge than the angels.

exercises.title: Gifts and Results
exercises.instructions: Match each gift or action with its result in Chapter 2.
exercises.question: What did each gift or action lead to?

matchingPairs.right: Humans have many skin colors.
Adam could learn and understand.
Adam could do good on earth.

correctAnswer.Allah’s teaching: Adam could do good on earth.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 2 gives three links: The angels collected soil from different parts of the earth, “That’s why humans have different skin colors”; Allah gave Adam “life and intellect to learn and understand”; and “He taught Adam (pbuh) everything he needed to do good on earth.”

feedback.correct: Well done. You followed the linking words: “That’s why”, “to learn” and “to do good”.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the linking words in Chapter 2: “That’s why …” in the first paragraph, and “to …” after “intellect” and after “taught” in the second paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Must Happen First?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read Allah’s words in Chapter 2. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: Allah told His angels, “After I have created Adam (pbuh) and given him life and knowledge, show respect to him.” When were the angels to show respect to Adam?
options: when his creation was complete and he had life and knowledge
while he was still being shaped from soil and had no life yet
before Allah created him, when the angels first heard the news
after Adam had lived on earth with his family for many years
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “After + have/has + past participle” (After I have created … and given …) shows an action that must be complete before the next action can happen. The instruction “show respect to him” comes second: first the creation and the gift of life and knowledge, then the respect.

feedback.correct: Correct. “After I have created … and given …” means the creation must be complete first.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verbs after “After”: “have created” and “given”. Are these actions finished or still going on when the angels show respect?

languageFocusExercises.title: Purpose, Sequence and Comparison
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 2 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word says why, which says what came next, and which compares?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Allah gave Adam (pbuh) life and intellect [blank] learn and understand. [blank], He taught Adam (pbuh) everything he needed to do good on earth. He gave Adam (pbuh) more knowledge [blank] the angels.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “To + base verb” gives the purpose of a gift: life and intellect were given so that Adam could learn and understand (not “for learn”). “Later” moves the account to the next stage. “More … than” compares two things; “more … as” is a common mistake.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed purpose, the next stage and a comparison.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2. Ask: Why was intellect given? When did the teaching happen? What is Adam’s knowledge compared with?

languageFocusExercises.title: Reason First or Result First?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write the missing words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say why humans have different skin colors?

transformItems.source: Then, Allah’s angels collected soil from different parts of the earth and Allah shaped Adam (pbuh). That’s why humans have different skin colors.
transformItems.frame: Humans have different skin colors [blank] Allah’s angels collected soil from different parts of the earth.

transformItems.source: Then, Allah’s angels collected soil from different parts of the earth and Allah shaped Adam (pbuh). That’s why humans have different skin colors.
transformItems.frame: Allah’s angels collected soil from different parts of the earth, [blank] humans have different skin colors.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “That’s why” starts a new sentence and points back to the reason in the sentence before. “Because” (or since / as) comes before the reason, so the result can come first. “So” (or which is why) joins the reason and the result in one sentence, with the reason first.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the cause-result meaning while changing the order.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: the result comes first, so you need a word that introduces a reason. Item 2: the reason comes first, so you need a word that introduces a result.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Connected Explanation
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about learning something new.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did you learn, and how?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: For example, you can introduce what a teacher said, explain why a learner received a tool, use “so” or “that’s why” for the result, and finish with a “more ... than” comparison.

feedback.correct: Keep the ideas connected so each sentence develops the same situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what someone told you: “Our teacher told us that …”
discussionPrompts.example: Our teacher told us that the science club would start a new project next week.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give a reason and a result: “…, so …” or “That’s why …”
discussionPrompts.example: We had never used the new microscope, so she showed us how it works first.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what for: “… to + verb”
discussionPrompts.example: Each of us looked at a leaf to learn how plants make their food.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Compare: “… was more … than …”
discussionPrompts.example: Learning with the microscope was more exciting than reading about it in a book.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Which four colors does the chapter give for the children of Adam?
beforeYouRead.quote: white, red, black and yellow in color

iCan: I can explain why humans have different skin colors.
I can give a reason and its result with “so” or “that’s why”.
I can explain a new learning situation in four sentences.

pages.title: Iblis’s Arrogance
pages.content:
All the angels thought that Adam (pbuh) was amazing. They all admired him and showed respect to him, but Iblis didn’t think so. Iblis thought that Adam was an unimportant being created from clay. Then Allah asked Iblis, “Why didn’t you respect Adam (pbuh)?” Iblis said, “I am better than Adam (pbuh). You created me from fire, and You created Adam (pbuh) from soil.” 

Iblis was arrogant. He thought he was more important and more valuable than Adam (pbuh) because he believed his origin was superior. Iblis did not think carefully and was wrong about Adam (pbuh). He couldn’t see and accept that Adam (pbuh) had perfect knowledge for the good of every creature of Allah, which made him more valuable. According to Satan, fire was superior to clay. However, in the sight of Allah, superiority or greatness did not come from race, color, or being a member of a certain group.

vocabulary.definition: Felt respect and approval for someone.
Too proud and sure of one’s own importance.
The point or material from which something begins.
The state of being considered better or higher.

hotspots.title: Fire and Soil
hotspots.description: Iblis compared the fire he was created from with the soil of Adam (pbuh).

hotspots.title: Equal in Allah’s Sight
hotspots.description: In the sight of Allah, superiority does not come from origin, race, color or group.

exercises.title: Iblis’s Mistake
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best explanation from Chapter 3.
exercises.question: Why was Iblis wrong to think that he was better than Adam?
options: Allah had created Adam from fire, and Iblis from soil.
Adam was already the first Messenger and the father of many children.
He judged by origin and could not see the value of Adam’s knowledge.
exercises.explanation: Iblis thought his origin was superior because he was created from fire. The narrator says he “couldn’t see and accept that Adam (pbuh) had perfect knowledge for the good of every creature of Allah, which made him more valuable,” and that greatness “did not come from race, color, or being a member of a certain group.”

feedback.correct: Right. Iblis looked only at what they were made of; the chapter says real value came from Adam’s knowledge.
feedback.incorrect: Compare what Iblis says about fire and soil with the second paragraph of Chapter 3. What could Iblis not see?

languageFocusExercises.title: Whose View Is It?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Is it a character’s view or the narrator’s words? Put each part in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who says it: A character, or the narrator?

items: All the angels thought that Adam (pbuh) was amazing.
Iblis believed his origin was superior
Iblis said, “I am better than Adam (pbuh).”
The angels all admired Adam and showed respect to him
Iblis was arrogant.
Iblis did not think carefully and was wrong about Adam (pbuh).

A character’s view (thought / believed /: All the angels thought that Adam (pbuh) was amazing.
Iblis believed his origin was superior
Iblis said, “I am better than Adam (pbuh).”
The narrator’s own statement: The angels all admired Adam and showed respect to him
Iblis did not think carefully and was wrong about Adam (pbuh).

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Verbs such as “thought that”, “believed” and “said” tell us that an idea belongs to a character. The narrator does not have to agree with it: Iblis believed his origin was superior, but the narrator tells us plainly that “Iblis was arrogant” and “was wrong about Adam”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the characters’ views from the narrator’s own statements.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a reporting verb (thought, believed, said). If there is one, the idea belongs to a character. If the sentence simply tells us what happened or what was true, it is the narrator.

languageFocusExercises.title: Comparing and Contrasting
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 3.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words compare, and which word starts a different view?

formChoices.sentence: He thought he was [choice] and more valuable than Adam (pbuh) …
According to Satan, fire was superior [choice] clay.
[choice], in the sight of Allah, superiority or greatness did not come from race, color, or being a member of a certain group.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Long adjectives such as “important” and “valuable” make the comparative with “more … than”, not with -er. “Superior” already has a comparing meaning, so it takes “to”, not “than”. “However” introduces a view that contrasts with the one before: Satan’s view against the view “in the sight of Allah”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the right comparative forms and the contrast marker.
feedback.incorrect: Check the second paragraph of Chapter 3. Notice “superior to” and ask whether the last sentence agrees with Satan’s view or contrasts with it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about Iblis and Adam?

errorItems.sentence: Iblis thought that Adam is an unimportant being created from clay.
They all admired him and showed respect to him, and Iblis didn’t think so.
He couldn’t see and accept that Adam (pbuh) had perfect knowledge for the good of every creature of Allah, what made him more valuable.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “thought that” in a past story, the reported belief stays in the past: “Iblis thought that Adam was …”. The narrator does not share this belief, so the present “is” is wrong. “But” shows that Iblis’s reaction was the opposite of everyone else’s. After a comma, “which” adds a comment about the whole idea before it (Adam’s perfect knowledge made him more valuable); “that” cannot follow a comma in this way, and “who” is for people.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the reported belief, the contrast and the added result.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with Chapter 3: Iblis’s belief in the first paragraph, the angels’ reaction, and the sentence that begins “He couldn’t see and accept …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Balanced Judgment
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about two people with different opinions.
languageFocusExercises.question: What does each person think, and what do you decide?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response can use “thought that” or “believed”, add a reason with “because”, make a comparison with “better/more ... than”, and introduce a contrasting conclusion with “but” or “however”.

feedback.correct: Keep each sentence connected to the same situation and make the contrast clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give one person’s view: “… thought that …”
discussionPrompts.example: Sara thought that our class trip should go to the museum.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give the reason: “because …”
discussionPrompts.example: She chose the museum because we could learn a lot about history there.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give another view and compare: “… is better than …”
discussionPrompts.example: Ali believed that the park was better than the museum on a sunny day.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what you decide: “However, …” or “But …”
discussionPrompts.example: However, after we heard both ideas, most of us decided to visit the museum in the morning and the park after lunch.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: How did all the angels feel about Adam (pbuh)?
beforeYouRead.quote: They all admired him and showed respect to him

iCan: I can explain why Iblis refused to respect Adam (pbuh).
I can compare two things with “better than” and “more … than”.
I can report two different opinions and give my conclusion.

pages.title: The Expulsion of Iblis
pages.content:
But Iblis continued saying he was right and the Creator was wrong. Allah said to Iblis, “Go away! You are far from My love and care.” Iblis got angry with Adam (pbuh) and hated him. He didn’t want Allah to be kind to Adam (pbuh). He thought that because of Adam (pbuh), Allah had put him far from His help. 

He waited for a chance to keep Adam (pbuh) away from Allah’s kindness, just as he himself was. Allah told Adam (pbuh) that Iblis was his enemy and warned him to be careful of Iblis.

vocabulary.definition: The One who brought all things into existence.
Disliked someone very strongly.
Someone who is hostile or wishes harm.
Paying attention to avoid danger or harm.

hotspots.title: Distance from Mercy
hotspots.description: Iblis was sent away from Allah’s love and care after he refused to respect Adam (pbuh).

hotspots.title: The Warning
hotspots.description: Allah warned Adam (pbuh) that Iblis was his enemy and told him to be careful.

exercises.title: Whom Did Iblis Blame?
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 4.
exercises.question: After Allah sent him away, Iblis blamed Adam, not himself.
exercises.explanation: Iblis “continued saying he was right.” He got angry with Adam and “thought that because of Adam (pbuh), Allah had put him far from His help.” So he blamed Adam, not himself.

feedback.correct: Correct. Iblis did not accept responsibility; he blamed Adam instead.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4 again. Look at the sentence that starts “He thought that because of …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Which Happened First?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: Allah said to Iblis, “Go away! …” Later in the paragraph we read: “He thought that … Allah had put him far from His help.” Why “had put” and not “put”?
options: Iblis was sent away at the same moment as he was thinking this.
Allah had already sent Iblis away before Iblis had this thought.
It shows something that was going to happen later.
It shows something that Iblis did again and again.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The past perfect (had + past participle) shows that one past event happened before another past event. First Allah sent Iblis away (“Go away!”); after that, Iblis thought about it and blamed Adam. “Had put” makes this order clear.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Had put” shows the earlier of two past events.
feedback.incorrect: Find “Go away!” in the first paragraph. Did that happen before or after Iblis’s thought about Adam?

languageFocusExercises.title: Verb Patterns and Reasons
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit after “continued” and “want”, and which gives a reason?

formChoices.sentence: But Iblis continued [choice] he was right and the Creator was wrong.
He didn’t want Allah [choice] kind to Adam (pbuh).
He thought that [choice] Adam (pbuh), Allah had put him far from His help.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Continue + -ing” (or continue + to + verb) shows that an action or claim goes on: Iblis did not stop saying he was right. “Want + person + to + verb” says what someone wants another person to do; English does not use “want that …”. “Because of” is followed by a noun (because of Adam); “because” is followed by a full clause with a subject and a verb.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose continue + -ing, want + person + to, and because of + noun.
feedback.incorrect: Check the first paragraph of Chapter 4. Remember: after “because of” comes a noun, and after “want Allah” comes “to + verb”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build Iblis’s Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to make the sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was Iblis waiting for?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Wait for a chance to + verb” says what someone is waiting to be able to do. “Keep + person + away from + something” means stop that person from being close to it; the person comes between “keep” and “away from”. “Just as he himself was” compares Adam’s possible future with Iblis’s own situation.

feedback.correct: Well done. You placed the person between “keep” and “away from”.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the person and the verb. Then: What was he waiting for? Put the person after “keep”, and finish with the comparison. Check the second paragraph of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Warning Situation
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about a bad habit and a warning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What does the person keep doing, and who warns them?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may use “continued + -ing”, “because of + noun”, “waited for a chance to ...”, “keep + object + away from ...”, and “warned + person + to be careful of ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the four sentences connected and make the reason and warning clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what someone kept doing: “… continued + -ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: Omar continued playing games on his phone late every night.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Give a reason: “Because of + thing, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Because of his tiredness, he often fell asleep in class.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what they waited for: “… waited for a chance to …”
discussionPrompts.example: During lessons, he only waited for a chance to play again in the break.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give the warning: “… warned him to be careful of …”
discussionPrompts.example: His teacher warned him to be careful of too much screen time.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What did Iblis not want Allah to do?
beforeYouRead.quote: He didn’t want Allah to be kind to Adam (pbuh).

iCan: I can explain why Iblis was sent away.
I can say that someone kept doing something and why.
I can write a short story with a clear warning.

groupTask.title: From Soil to the Warning

roles.name: Chapter 1 Expert
roles.job: You teach what Allah told the angels before He created Adam (pbuh).

roles.name: Chapter 2 Expert
roles.job: You teach how Adam (pbuh) was shaped and what Allah gave him.

roles.name: Chapter 3 Expert
roles.job: You teach why Iblis refused to respect Adam (pbuh).

roles.name: Chapter 4 Expert
roles.job: You teach why Iblis was sent away and what Allah told Adam (pbuh).

steps: Read your chapter again and find two important facts.
Teach your facts to the group in your own words, then read the sentence from the book for each one. For example: “He gave Adam (pbuh) more knowledge than the angels.”
Listen to the others and write one fact from each chapter in the right order.
Together, finish this sentence with two reasons from the book: “Iblis became an enemy of Adam (pbuh) because …”. For example, Iblis said, “I am better than Adam (pbuh).”
groupTask.share: Each group reads its four facts in order and its two reasons, and shows the sentence from the book for each reason.
groupTask.solo: Read Chapters 1–4 again and write one fact from each chapter on a card. Then copy the sentence that shows how Allah “warned him to be careful of Iblis”.

pages.title: Life in Paradise and the Warning
pages.content:
Adam was in Paradise, but he started to feel lonely. Allah gave him a wife called Eve (Hawwa) to be his companion. They began living in Paradise. It was more wonderful than we can imagine. All the blessings in Paradise were for them. 

Allah only asked them not to go near one tree. When Adam (pbuh) and Eve were happy in Paradise, Iblis came near them pretending to be their friend. It was a big lie. He whispered to them that if they ate from that one tree, they would never die.

vocabulary.definition: Unhappy because one is without companionship.
Someone who spends time with another person and shares their life.
Good things or gifts for which people are thankful.
Spoke very quietly so that others could not hear.

hotspots.title: A Companion for Adam
hotspots.description: Allah gave Adam (pbuh) a wife, Eve, and they lived together among the blessings of Paradise.

hotspots.title: The One Tree
hotspots.description: Iblis came to them pretending to be their friend and whispered a lie about the tree.

exercises.title: A False Friend
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapters 4 and 5.
exercises.question: Why did Iblis come to Adam and Eve pretending to be their friend?
options: He wanted to say sorry to Adam for his arrogance.
He wanted them to trust him and believe his lie about the tree.
He wanted to keep Adam company because Adam felt lonely.
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 4 Iblis waits “for a chance to keep Adam (pbuh) away from Allah’s kindness.” In Chapter 5 he pretends to be their friend – “It was a big lie” – and whispers that if they eat from the tree, they will never die.

feedback.correct: Yes. A friendly face helped him make them believe his lie. This is why a friendly claim still needs checking.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 5 and the end of Chapter 4. What was Iblis waiting for, and what did he whisper?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Do These Phrases Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each phrase from Chapter 5 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these phrases tell us about life in Paradise and about Iblis?

matchingPairs.right: a partner who had this name
so that he had someone to share his life with

matchingPairs.left: more wonderful than we can imagine
matchingPairs.right: better than anything people can picture
acting as if he cared about them, but not really
said very quietly and secretly

correctAnswer.a wife called Eve (Hawwa): a partner who had this name
correctAnswer.to be his companion: so that he had someone to share his life with
correctAnswer.more wonderful than we can imagine: better than anything people can picture
correctAnswer.pretending to be their friend: acting as if he cared about them, but not really

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Called + name” gives a person’s name. “To be + role” gives the purpose of a gift or action. “More … than we can imagine” compares Paradise with the limit of human imagination. “Pretend to be” means to act as if something is true when it is not; the chapter adds, “It was a big lie.”

feedback.correct: Correct. You understood how each phrase adds meaning to the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 5 again and look at the words around each phrase, for example “It was a big lie” after “pretending to be their friend”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Beginnings and a Restriction
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words come after “started”, “began” and “asked them”?

formChoices.sentence: Adam was in Paradise, but he started [choice] lonely.
They began [choice] in Paradise.
Allah only asked them [choice] near one tree.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Start” and “begin” are followed by “to + verb” or “-ing” (started to feel, began living). Only the first verb shows the past; the second verb does not change. To report a negative request, use ask + person + not to + verb: “asked them not to go”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the right verb patterns for a beginning and a reported restriction.
feedback.incorrect: Check Chapter 5: after “started” and “began”, the verb does not take the past form. For a request not to do something, “not” comes before “to”.

languageFocusExercises.title: From Reported Words to Direct Words
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write Iblis’s own words. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Iblis say to them?

transformItems.source: He whispered to them that if they ate from that one tree, they would never die.
transformItems.frame: He whispered to them, “If you eat from that one tree, you [blank] die.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: In direct words about the future, Iblis would use “If + present, … will + verb”: “If you eat …, you will never die.” When the narrator reports it in a past story, the verbs move back: eat → ate, will → would. The chapter makes clear that this claim was false: “It was a big lie.”

feedback.correct: Well done. You changed the reported claim back into direct words.
feedback.incorrect: In direct speech the verbs move forward again: “ate” becomes “eat”, and “would” becomes “will”. Keep the word “never”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a New Advice Situation
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about someone who starts something new.
languageFocusExercises.question: What starts, what is not allowed, and what could happen?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may use “started to ...”, “began + -ing”, “more ... than ...”, “asked + person + not to ...”, “when ...”, and an “if ... would ...” relationship.

feedback.correct: Keep the sentences connected and make the restriction and result easy to follow.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what started: “… started to …” or “… began + -ing”
discussionPrompts.example: When the new school year began, Lina started to feel nervous about the long bus ride.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Compare: “… was more … than …”
discussionPrompts.example: But her new school was bigger and more beautiful than her old one.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what someone asked: “… asked her not to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Her mother asked her not to use her phone on the bus.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what would happen: “If …, … would …”
discussionPrompts.example: If she listened to her mother, she would see the city and make new friends on the way.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: Who were all the blessings in Paradise for?
beforeYouRead.quote: All the blessings in Paradise were for them.

iCan: I can describe life in Paradise and the one rule.
I can say what someone asked another person not to do.
I can say what would happen if someone did something.

pages.title: Satan’s lies and Adam’s Departure from Paradise
pages.content:
Eventually, Iblis managed to trick them. He convinced them to believe his lies, and they forgot the warning Allah had given them. Adam stretched out his hand, picked one of the fruits and offered it to Eve. They both ate of the forbidden tree. 

When Adam finished eating, he felt that his heart was filled with pain, sadness and shame. The surrounding atmosphere changed and the internal harmony ceased. 

When they tasted the fruit, their private parts became visible. Adam (pbuh) saw that he and his wife had no clothes on, so they both started cutting tree leaves in Paradise to cover themselves. They hurried to hide their private parts because a sense of shame (haya) is part of inborn human nature and nakedness is against creation.

vocabulary.definition: Not allowed by a rule or command.
A painful feeling connected with awareness of wrong behavior.
Able to be seen.
Present naturally from birth.

hotspots.title: The Forbidden Tree
hotspots.description: Adam (pbuh) and Eve ate from the tree after they believed Iblis’s lies.

hotspots.title: Modesty
hotspots.description: Adam (pbuh) and Eve quickly covered themselves with leaves because a sense of shame is part of human nature.

exercises.title: Covering with Leaves
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 6.
exercises.question: Why did Adam and Eve hurry to cover themselves with leaves?
options: A sense of shame (haya) is part of inborn human nature.
Iblis told them to hide from Allah.
They had to protect themselves from dangers in the wild.
exercises.explanation: The last sentence of Chapter 6 says: “They hurried to hide their private parts because a sense of shame (haya) is part of inborn human nature and nakedness is against creation.” Dangers in the wild come later, on earth (Chapter 8).

feedback.correct: Right. The chapter explains their reaction with haya, a feeling every human is born with.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 6 and find the word “because”.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Managed to” Tell Us?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the first sentence of Chapter 6. Then choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Eventually, Iblis managed to trick them.” What do “eventually” and “managed to” tell us together?
options: Iblis tricked them easily and quickly, the very first time he tried.
Iblis tried to trick them, but he did not succeed.
Iblis had tried for some time, and in the end he succeeded.
Iblis was ordered to trick them, and he did what he was told.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Manage to + verb” means to succeed in doing something difficult. “Eventually” means “in the end, after some time”. Together they show that Iblis’s success came only after effort. In the same paragraph, the past perfect “the warning Allah had given them” shows that the warning came before they forgot it.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Managed to” shows success after difficulty, and “eventually” shows it came in the end.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the first word of Chapter 6, “Eventually”. Does it mean “at once” or “in the end”? Then ask what “managed to” adds.

languageFocusExercises.title: Put the Events in Order
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 6 in the right order.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened after Iblis tricked them?

sequencingItems.text: Iblis convinced Adam and Eve to believe his lies, …
Adam stretched out his hand, picked one of the fruits and offered it to Eve.
Adam and Eve both ate of the forbidden tree.
When Adam finished eating, he felt that his heart was filled with pain, sadness and shame.
Adam and Eve hurried to hide their private parts …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The chapter tells the events in time order. A list of past simple verbs (stretched out, picked, offered) gives actions one after another. The time clause “When Adam finished eating” marks the point after which the feeling came, and the final actions show the reaction to what they saw.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the actions, the time clause and the reaction in order.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 6 again. What had to happen before Adam picked the fruit? What does “When Adam finished eating” tell you about the order?

languageFocusExercises.title: Result, Purpose and Reason
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 6 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words show a result, a purpose and a reason?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Adam (pbuh) saw that he and his wife had no clothes on, [blank] they both started cutting tree leaves in Paradise [blank] cover themselves. They hurried to hide their private parts [blank] a sense of shame (haya) is part of inborn human nature …
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “So” introduces a result: They saw they had no clothes on, so they started cutting leaves. “To + verb” gives the purpose of the action (to cover themselves), not “for cover”. “Because” introduces a reason with a full clause; “because of” needs a noun.

feedback.correct: Correct. You linked the result, the purpose and the reason.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 6. Ask: What happened as a result? Why did they cut leaves? Why did they hurry?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Consequence Chain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about someone who forgets good advice.
languageFocusExercises.question: What advice was forgotten, and what happened?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may use “managed to ...”, “convinced + person + to ...”, “had + past participle”, “when ...”, “became ...”, “so ...”, “to + verb” for purpose, and “because ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sequence easy to follow and make the purpose and cause explicit.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the earlier advice: “… had told them to …”
discussionPrompts.example: The coach had told the players to drink water during the long training.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say who got him to do it: “… convinced him to …”
discussionPrompts.example: But a classmate convinced Yusuf to skip the water break and keep playing.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Show a change: “Soon he became …, so …”
discussionPrompts.example: Soon he became very tired, so he had to sit down.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what he did and why: “He … to … because …”
discussionPrompts.example: He drank some water to feel better because he finally remembered the coach’s advice.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What changed around Adam (pbuh) after he ate the fruit?

iCan: I can tell what happened when Adam (pbuh) and Eve ate the fruit.
I can talk about something that happened before another past event.
I can write a short chain of events and results.

pages.title: Forgiveness and Repentance
pages.content:
Adam (pbuh) bowed down and cried, “Forgiveness! Forgiveness!” Allah asked, “Are you running away from Me?” Adam (pbuh) replied, “No, my Lord, but I am shy of You.” 

They made a mistake, but it wasn’t on purpose. They were very sad about their wrong action. They said sorry to Allah, learned from their mistake and decided never to repeat it. They wanted Allah to pardon them. 

On the other hand, Iblis chose an opposite path. He never admitted he was wrong because he was arrogant. Arrogance is the biggest barrier to acting the right way and distinguishing between right and wrong, good and bad. 

Allah pardoned both Adam (pbuh) and Eve and put them on earth to live there. Allah taught them and gave them everything they needed to rule on earth. They were the rulers of planet Earth. They would direct, control and make everything better on the planet.

vocabulary.definition: Completely different, or going in the other direction.
To forgive someone for a wrong action.
Something that prevents progress or clear understanding.
Recognizing the difference between things.

hotspots.title: Mistake and Pardon
hotspots.description: Adam (pbuh) and Eve admitted their mistake, learned from it and asked Allah to forgive them.

hotspots.title: Arrogance as a Barrier
hotspots.description: Iblis never admitted he was wrong because his arrogance stopped him.

exercises.title: Two Different Paths
exercises.instructions: Match each part with what Chapter 7 says about it.
exercises.question: How does Chapter 7 compare two ways of reacting to a mistake?

matchingPairs.right: a sincere apology and a wish to be pardoned
a refusal ever to admit being in the wrong
the biggest barrier to telling good from bad

correctAnswer.Adam and Eve: a sincere apology and a wish to be pardoned
correctAnswer.Iblis: a refusal ever to admit being in the wrong
correctAnswer.Arrogance: the biggest barrier to telling good from bad

exercises.explanation: Adam and Eve “said sorry to Allah” and “wanted Allah to pardon them.” Iblis “never admitted he was wrong because he was arrogant.” The chapter calls arrogance “the biggest barrier to acting the right way and distinguishing between right and wrong, good and bad.” In the end, “Allah pardoned both Adam (pbuh) and Eve.”

feedback.correct: Well done. Adam and Eve took responsibility, but Iblis’s arrogance kept him on the opposite path.
feedback.incorrect: Use the second paragraph of Chapter 7 for Adam and Eve, and the third paragraph (“On the other hand …”) for Iblis and arrogance.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words for Responsibility
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each phrase from Chapter 7 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these phrases tell us about Adam, Eve and Iblis?

matchingPairs.right: they did not do it deliberately
understood a lesson because of what went wrong
forgive
took a completely different direction
the thing that stops people most

correctAnswer.it wasn’t on purpose: they did not do it deliberately
correctAnswer.learned from their mistake: understood a lesson because of what went wrong
correctAnswer.the biggest barrier: the thing that stops people most

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “On purpose” means deliberately, so “it wasn’t on purpose” separates the mistake from a planned wrong. “Learn from + mistake” means to take a lesson from it. “Pardon” is a formal word for “forgive”. “An opposite path” and “the biggest barrier” help the chapter contrast Adam and Eve’s response with Iblis’s arrogance.

feedback.correct: Correct. These phrases show how the chapter talks about responsibility.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 7 again and use the words around each phrase to find its meaning.

languageFocusExercises.title: Linking Two Responses
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 7 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words show a difference, and which gives a reason?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: They made a mistake, [blank] it wasn’t on purpose. … [blank], Iblis chose an opposite path. He never admitted he was wrong [blank] he was arrogant.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “But” limits the first idea inside one sentence: There was a mistake, but it was not intentional. “On the other hand” starts a new part of the text and moves to a contrasting person or path. “Because” gives the reason with a full clause (he was arrogant); “because of” would need a noun.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the right links for contrast and reason.
feedback.incorrect: Ask for each gap: Does it limit the first idea, move to a different person’s path, or give a reason? Then check Chapter 7.

languageFocusExercises.title: Decision, Wish and Purpose
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 7.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit after “decided never” and “wanted Allah”, and which says what for?

formChoices.sentence: They said sorry to Allah, learned from their mistake and decided never [choice] it.
They wanted Allah [choice] them.
Allah pardoned both Adam (pbuh) and Eve and put them on earth [choice] there.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Decide (never) to + verb” expresses a decision about the future. “Want + person + to + verb” says what someone wants another person to do. “To + verb” after an action gives its purpose: they were put on earth to live there, not “for live”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each of these patterns uses “to + base verb”.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the second and fourth paragraphs of Chapter 7. After “decided never”, “wanted Allah” and “on earth”, which form do you find?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Repair-and-Responsibility Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about someone who puts a mistake right.
languageFocusExercises.question: What went wrong, and how did the person fix it?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may include “not on purpose”, “was/were sad about ...”, “learned from ...”, “decided never to ...”, “wanted + person + to ...”, “because ...”, “on the other hand ...”, “to + verb” for purpose, or “would ...” for an expected later action.

feedback.correct: Keep the four sentences connected so the intention, response, reason, and next responsibility are easy to follow.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what went wrong: “…, but it wasn’t on purpose.”
discussionPrompts.example: Mariam dropped her heavy bag on her friend’s pencil case and broke it, but it wasn’t on purpose.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what the person did and learned: “She said sorry and learned to …”
discussionPrompts.example: She said sorry at once and learned to be more careful with other people’s things.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a reason and a decision: “Because …, she decided never to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Because she wanted to be fair, she decided never to put her bag on a friend’s desk again.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say the next step: “She … to …” or “She would …”
discussionPrompts.example: She saved her pocket money to buy her friend a new pencil case, and she would be more careful in the future.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What did Adam (pbuh) ask Allah for?

iCan: I can explain how Adam (pbuh) and Eve asked for forgiveness.
I can say what someone decided never to do again.
I can write how someone puts a mistake right.

pages.title: Struggle and Survival on Earth
pages.content:
They would use land to grow crops and keep animals. They would build buildings for shelter, protect nature and help the weak. 

Adam (pbuh) and Eve left Paradise and arrived on earth. On earth, they had to struggle to survive and work hard to keep themselves alive. In addition, they had to protect themselves with clothes and weapons and protect themselves from dangers in the wild. 

Iblis followed Adam (pbuh), Eve and their children to earth. He was still there because he wanted people not to remember Allah. Adam (pbuh) and Eve lived on earth for many years. They had both good and difficult times and they had many children. We all come from their children.

vocabulary.definition: A place that gives protection from danger or weather.
To make a strong effort during difficulty.
To continue to live despite difficulty or danger.
Objects used for protection or fighting.

hotspots.title: Work on Earth
hotspots.description: On earth, Adam (pbuh) and Eve would grow crops, keep animals, build shelters, protect nature and help the weak.

hotspots.title: Protection from Danger
hotspots.description: Adam (pbuh) and Eve had to work hard and protect themselves with clothes and weapons.

exercises.title: From Paradise to Earth
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapters 5 and 8.
exercises.question: Life on earth was very different for Adam and Eve from their life in Paradise.
exercises.explanation: In Paradise “All the blessings in Paradise were for them” (Chapter 5). On earth “they had to struggle to survive and work hard to keep themselves alive,” and they had to protect themselves “from dangers in the wild” (Chapter 8).

feedback.correct: Correct. In Paradise everything was given to them; on earth they had to work, struggle and protect themselves.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the first paragraph of Chapter 5 with the second paragraph of Chapter 8. Was life easy in both places?

languageFocusExercises.title: Why, With What, How Long?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Does it say why, with what, or how long? Put each part in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: What does each phrase tell us: why, with what, or how long?

items: … use land to grow crops and keep animals.
… build buildings for shelter …
… work hard to keep themselves alive.
… protect themselves with clothes and weapons …
Adam (pbuh) and Eve lived on earth for many years.

Why? (purpose): … use land to grow crops and keep animals.
… work hard to keep themselves alive.
With what? (means): … protect themselves with clothes and weapons …
How long? (time): Adam (pbuh) and Eve lived on earth for many years.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “To + verb” (to grow, to keep) gives the purpose of an action. “For + noun” can also give a purpose (for shelter), but “for + a period of time” (for many years) tells us how long. “With + noun” (with clothes and weapons) tells us what people used to do something.

feedback.correct: Correct. You noticed that “for” can show a purpose or a length of time.
feedback.incorrect: Ask a question about each phrase: Why did they do it? What did they use? How long did it last? Notice that “shelter” is a purpose, but “many years” is a time.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about life on earth and Iblis?

errorItems.sentence: They will use land to grow crops and keep animals.
On earth, they had to struggle for survive and work hard to keep themselves alive.
He was still there because he wanted people don’t remember Allah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story is told in the past, so a role that was still ahead of Adam and Eve is described with “would + verb”, not “will”. Purpose is “to + verb” (to survive), not “for + verb”. In the negative, “want + person + to” becomes “want + person + not to + verb”: he wanted people not to remember Allah.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed “would”, the purpose infinitive and the negative “want” pattern.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with Chapter 8: the first sentence of the chapter, the second paragraph, and the sentence about Iblis in the third paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Necessity and Addition
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 8 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word adds more, which shows a need, and which joins two things?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: [blank], they [blank] protect themselves with clothes and weapons and protect themselves from dangers in the wild. … They had [blank] good and difficult times and they had many children.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “In addition” adds another point of the same kind: One more thing they needed to do. “Had to + verb” is the past of “must” when it means necessity; “must” is not used for the past. “Both … and …” joins two things and says that each one is true: Their life had good times and difficult times.

feedback.correct: Correct. You added a need, showed past necessity and joined two experiences.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 8. Does the first sentence add or contrast? Is the story in the past? Which word goes with “… and …”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a New Responsibility Account
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about people starting life in a hard new place.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do the people have to do in their new place?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may use “would + verb” for an expected role, “had to + verb” for necessity, “to + verb” for purpose, “in addition” to add another demand, “with + noun” for means, “because + clause” for cause, or “for + period” for duration.

feedback.correct: Keep the four sentences connected so the role, necessity, purpose, and reason form one coherent account.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what the people would do: “They would …”
discussionPrompts.example: At the mountain camp, the new students would cook, clean and look after the garden.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what they had to do and why: “They had to … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: They had to collect wood every morning to keep the fire burning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Add more: “In addition, …” and “with + thing”
discussionPrompts.example: In addition, they needed fresh water, so they carried it from the river with big bottles.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give a reason: “because …” and how long: “for …”
discussionPrompts.example: They worked hard because life at the camp was not easy, and they stayed there for two weeks.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What did they protect themselves with on earth?
beforeYouRead.quote: they had to protect themselves with clothes and weapons

iCan: I can describe the work Adam (pbuh) and Eve did on earth.
I can say what people had to do and why.
I can describe life in a difficult new place.

groupTask.title: History Radio Show: From Paradise to Earth

roles.name: Reporter
roles.job: You ask the historian questions about Chapters 5–8.

roles.name: Historian
roles.job: You answer with facts from the book.

roles.name: Helper
roles.job: You find the sentence in the book when the historian needs help.

roles.name: Listener
roles.job: You ask one last question and say thank you.

steps: Together, write four questions, like “What was the one thing Allah asked them not to do?” or “What did they have to do on earth?”
The Reporter says hello to the listeners and asks the questions.
The Historian answers in short sentences: “The book says …”. For example, the book says they “had to struggle to survive and work hard to keep themselves alive”.
Nobody speaks as a person from the story; the Historian only tells the listeners what the book says about them.
groupTask.share: Each group performs its show and says one important fact it learned.
groupTask.solo: Write three questions about Chapters 5–8 and answer each one with a sentence from the book.

pages.title: The First Messenger and the Path of Guidance
pages.content:
At that time, there was no community. After a period of time, when a community formed, Adam (pbuh) became the first Messenger of Allah. Thus, he became the first human, the first father, and the first messenger of Islam. He started teaching people to live righteously and act honestly. He showed the way to do good, avoid evil and always keep Allah in their hearts and minds. 

Allah never stopped sending messengers and sacred texts to remind people of Him. Adam (pbuh) and Eve taught their children to pray only to Allah and be aware of Iblis and his tricks because Iblis was their enemy, not their friend. 

Years later, after the death of Adam (pbuh), Allah sent many other messengers to show people the right path and the ways to stay away from Iblis. All the messengers followed the same path. They wanted people to keep Allah in their minds because if people forget Allah, they lose the meaning and purpose of life.

vocabulary.definition: A group of people living or acting together.
In a morally right way.
Connected with religion and deserving special respect.
The reason why something exists or is done.

hotspots.title: The First Community
hotspots.description: When a community formed, Adam (pbuh) became the first Messenger and taught people to live righteously.

hotspots.title: Messengers and Sacred Texts
hotspots.description: Allah kept sending messengers and sacred texts to remind people of Him and the right path.

exercises.title: Why Remember Allah?
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 9.
exercises.question: All the messengers wanted people to keep Allah in their minds. What reason does the chapter give?
options: Without this, people could not grow crops or build shelters.
Otherwise, Allah would stop sending messengers to them.
If people forget Allah, they lose the meaning and purpose of life.
exercises.explanation: The last sentence of Chapter 9 says the messengers wanted people to keep Allah in their minds “because if people forget Allah, they lose the meaning and purpose of life.” The chapter also says: “Allah never stopped sending messengers and sacred texts to remind people of Him.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Remembering Allah gives life its meaning and purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 9 again and find the word “because”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Stopped Doing or Stopped to Do?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 9. Then decide: True or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “Allah never stopped sending messengers and sacred texts to remind people of Him.” True or false: This means the same as “Allah never stopped to send messengers.”
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Stop + -ing” means that an activity ends: “never stopped sending” means the sending went on and never ended. “Stop + to + verb” means to pause one activity in order to do something else. So the two sentences have different meanings, and only “never stopped sending” fits the chapter.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Never stopped sending” means the sending continued all the time.
feedback.incorrect: Compare “I stopped eating” (I ended the activity) with “I stopped to eat” (I paused something else in order to eat). Which one matches the chapter’s meaning?

languageFocusExercises.title: Follow the Time Markers
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 9 in order. The time words can help.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened before and after Adam (pbuh) became a Messenger?

sequencingItems.text: At that time, there was no community.
After a period of time, when a community formed, Adam (pbuh) became the first Messenger of Allah.
Thus, he became the first human, the first father, and the first messenger of Islam.
Years later, after the death of Adam (pbuh), Allah sent many other messengers …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “At that time” describes the situation at the start. “After a period of time, when …” moves to a later stage, and “became” shows Adam’s new role. “Thus” draws a conclusion from what came before. “Years later, after the death of …” jumps forward to a much later time.

feedback.correct: Correct. The time markers lead you through the stages of the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the first words of each part. Which describes the starting situation, which a later stage, which a conclusion, and which a time long after?

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about teaching people?

errorItems.sentence: He started teaching people live righteously and act honestly.
… Allah sent many other messengers for show people the right path and the ways to stay away from Iblis.
They wanted people to keep Allah in their minds because if people will forget Allah, they lose the meaning and purpose of life.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Teach + person + to + verb” says what someone learns to do: teaching people to live righteously. “To + verb” after an action gives its purpose: messengers were sent to show the right path. In an if-clause about something that is generally true, use the present simple, not “will”: “if people forget Allah, they lose …”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the teaching pattern, the purpose and the if-clause.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with Chapter 9: the first paragraph, and the last paragraph that begins “Years later …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Guidance Paragraph
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about someone who starts to lead a group.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does the new leader guide the group?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may use “after ... / when ...”, “became ...”, “started teaching ... to ...”, “never stopped + -ing”, “to + verb” for purpose, “wanted + person + to ...”, or “if + present, present” for a general result.

feedback.correct: Keep the four sentences connected so the role change, teaching, purpose, and result form one coherent paragraph.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the new role: “After …, … became …”
discussionPrompts.example: After our old captain left the school, Hana became the leader of the football team.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what they taught: “… started teaching … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: She started teaching the young players to pass the ball to each other.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what they wanted: “… wanted everyone to …”
discussionPrompts.example: She wanted everyone to feel part of the team.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what went on: “… never stopped + -ing” or “If …, …”
discussionPrompts.example: She never stopped encouraging them, even when they lost a match.

beforeYouRead.question: Find it fast: What did Adam (pbuh) start teaching people?
options: to live righteously and act honestly
beforeYouRead.quote: He started teaching people to live righteously and act honestly.

iCan: I can explain how Adam (pbuh) became the first Messenger.
I can say when something began and that it never stopped.
I can write about someone who guides a group.

pages.title: The Two Sons: Habil and Qabil
pages.content:
Adam (pbuh) and Eve had two sons, Habil and Qabil. The children grew up to be strong and healthy young adults. They were very different. Habil was kind, gentle and loved taking care of animals. Qabil was mostly jealous. When they grew up, Habil became a shepherd. He kept cows, sheep and other animals. Qabil was a farmer. He worked on the farm and grew crops. 

One day, they were in a serious disagreement. To solve the problem, they had to make an offering to Allah. Habil brought his best and healthiest sheep as a gift for Allah, but Qabil brought just a handful of his crops that were not very valuable. Qabil didn’t care about pleasing Allah and his father Adam (pbuh). However, real goodness is giving out the best and the most loved.

vocabulary.definition: Unhappy because someone else has something one wants.
A person who takes care of sheep or other animals.
A serious difference of opinion.
A gift or sacrifice made to show devotion.

hotspots.title: Two Different Brothers
hotspots.description: Habil and Qabil grew up with different characters: Habil became a shepherd and Qabil a farmer.

hotspots.title: The Two Offerings
hotspots.description: To solve their disagreement, Habil offered his best sheep, but Qabil brought only a handful of poor crops.

exercises.title: What the Offering Shows
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the best answer from Chapter 10.
exercises.question: What does Qabil’s offering show about him?
options: He did not care about pleasing Allah and his father.
He had nothing better to give because he was a farmer.
He wanted to give Allah the thing he loved most.
exercises.explanation: Habil brought “his best and healthiest sheep,” but Qabil brought “just a handful of his crops that were not very valuable.” The chapter explains: “Qabil didn’t care about pleasing Allah and his father Adam (pbuh).” Being a farmer was not the problem; the problem was his intention.

feedback.correct: Right. The small gift showed that he did not really care. Real goodness is giving the best.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the two gifts in the second paragraph, then read the sentence about Qabil that comes after them.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Do These Phrases Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each phrase from Chapter 10 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these phrases tell us about the two brothers?

matchingPairs.right: developed into, as they got older
usually unhappy when others had good things
a big argument
only a small amount of

correctAnswer.grew up to be: developed into, as they got older
correctAnswer.mostly jealous: usually unhappy when others had good things

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Grow up to be + description” tells us what a child became as an adult. “Mostly” means “most of the time”. “Just” in “just a handful of” means “only” and makes the amount sound small, which contrasts with Habil’s “best and healthiest sheep”.

feedback.correct: Correct. These phrases help the chapter describe and contrast the brothers.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 10 again and use the words around each phrase. For example, what does “just” add before “a handful of his crops that were not very valuable”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Roles, Obligation and the Best Gift
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 10.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words show a new job, what they had to do, and the best?

formChoices.sentence: When they grew up, Habil [choice] a shepherd.
To solve the problem, they [choice] make an offering to Allah.
Habil brought his [choice] and healthiest sheep as a gift for Allah, …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Become” is irregular: become – became – become, so the past simple is “became”. “Had to” is the past form for a necessary action; “must” is not used for the past. “Good – better – best”: “best” is the superlative, and it matches “healthiest” in the same phrase.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the past form, the past obligation and the superlative.
feedback.incorrect: Check Chapter 10: the story is in the past, and “best” goes together with “healthiest”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sentences about Habil and Qabil?

errorItems.sentence: Habil was kind, gentle and loved take care of animals.
… as a gift for Allah, and Qabil brought just a handful of his crops that were not very valuable.
Qabil didn’t care about please Allah and his father Adam (pbuh).

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Love” can be followed by -ing (or to + verb), so “loved taking care of animals” is correct. “But” shows the contrast between the two gifts: Habil’s best sheep and Qabil’s crops that were not very valuable. After a preposition such as “about”, use the -ing form: “care about pleasing”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the verb patterns and the contrast.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each sentence with Chapter 10. Remember: after a preposition (about, of, in) the verb takes -ing.

languageFocusExercises.title: Compare Two Choices
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four sentences about two people who do the same job differently.
languageFocusExercises.question: How are the two people different?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response may use “when ... grew up”, “became ...”, “to + verb” for purpose, “had to ...”, “but/while/however” for contrast, “didn’t care about + -ing”, and a pattern such as “real responsibility is + -ing ...” to express a general principle.

feedback.correct: Keep the four sentences connected so the contrast grows naturally from the shared task.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Name the two people and their role: “When …, … became …”
discussionPrompts.example: When the school garden opened, Ahmed and Layla became its first helpers.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what they had to do and why: “To …, they had to …”
discussionPrompts.example: To make the garden beautiful, they had to plant flowers every Monday.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Show the difference: “…, while …” or “… but …”
discussionPrompts.example: Ahmed chose the strongest and healthiest plants, while Layla only planted the old ones that nobody wanted.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give a lesson: “Real … is + -ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: Real care is giving your best effort to every task.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. What did Habil bring as a gift for Allah?
beforeYouRead.quote: Habil brought his best and healthiest sheep

iCan: I can compare the offerings of Habil and Qabil.
I can show a difference with “but” or “while”.
I can compare two people who do the same task in different ways.

pages.title: The First Conflict and the Raven
pages.content: Allah accepted Habil’s offering because he gave from his heart. Qabil’s face became very dark with anger, and he said, “I will kill you.” When Habil heard this, he said, “I won’t fight back and harm you. You are my brother, and I fear Allah.” Qabil started fighting with his brother and killed him. Soon, Qabil’s anger cooled, and he felt very sad. He also started to panic. He said, “I killed my brother. I did the worst thing in life. Now I don’t know what I should do with his dead body.” Then Allah sent a raven that landed near Qabil and started digging the ground. It showed Qabil the way to put his brother’s dead body in the pit. Qabil cried and said, “I am worse than this raven. I cannot hide my brother’s dead body.”

vocabulary.definition: To hurt or damage someone or something.
To suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think calmly.
A large black bird.
Making a hole in the ground.

hotspots.title: Brother Against Brother
hotspots.description: Qabil attacked and killed Habil, even though Habil refused to fight back.

hotspots.title: A Lesson from a Bird
hotspots.description: Allah sent a raven that dug the ground and showed Qabil how to put his brother’s body in a pit.

exercises.title: From Anger to Regret
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 11 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happens first, next and last in Chapter 11?

sequencingItems.text: Allah accepts Habil’s offering.
Habil says he will not fight back because he fears Allah.
Qabil’s anger cools, and he feels very sad.
A raven lands near Qabil and digs the ground.
Qabil says, “I am worse than this raven.”

exercises.explanation: The chapter moves from the accepted offering to Qabil’s threat and Habil’s calm answer, then to Qabil’s sadness and panic after he killed his brother, then to the raven that Allah sent, and finally to Qabil’s words: “I am worse than this raven.”

feedback.correct: Well done. You followed the chain from jealousy and anger to regret.
feedback.incorrect: Follow Chapter 11 from its first sentence to its last. The raven comes only after Qabil does not know what to do.

languageFocusExercises.title: Future, Past or Now?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Future, past or now? Put each spoken line in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is each line about the future, the past or now?

dragDropGroups.group: The future: A threat or a refusal
items: “I will kill you.”
“I won’t fight back and harm you.”

dragDropGroups.group: The past: Admitting what he did
items: “I killed my brother.”
“I did the worst thing in life.”

dragDropGroups.group: Now: A present judgment or inability
items: “I am worse than this raven.”
“I cannot hide my brother’s dead body.”

The future: A threat or a refusal: “I won’t fight back and harm you.”
The past: Admitting what he did: “I did the worst thing in life.”
Now: A present judgment or inability: “I cannot hide my brother’s dead body.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Will” and “won’t” look to the future: Here “will” is a threat and “won’t” is a firm refusal. The past simple (killed, did) admits finished actions. The present (am, cannot) describes how Qabil sees himself and what he is unable to do at that moment. “Worst” compares with everything (the superlative); “worse than” compares two things.

feedback.correct: Correct. You connected each verb form with the time it talks about.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb in each quotation: will / won’t, killed / did, or am / cannot. Which time does each one point to?

languageFocusExercises.title: Reason, Beginning and Guidance
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 11.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word gives a reason, and which words come after “started” and “the way”?

formChoices.sentence: Allah accepted Habil’s offering [choice] he gave from his heart.
He also started [choice].
It showed Qabil the way [choice] his brother’s dead body in the pit.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Because” is followed by a full clause (he gave from his heart); “because of” needs a noun. “Start + to + verb” (or -ing) shows the beginning of a feeling or action. “Show someone the way to + verb” explains how to do something: the raven showed Qabil how to put the body in the ground.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the reason word, the verb pattern after “started” and the guidance pattern.
feedback.incorrect: Check Chapter 11. Is a full clause or a noun after the reason word? After “started”, the verb does not take the past form.

languageFocusExercises.title: Report What Qabil Said
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Report Qabil’s words. Write the missing words.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Qabil admit, and what did he not know?

transformItems.frame: Qabil admitted that he [blank] his brother.

transformItems.source: “Now I don’t know what I should do with his dead body.”
transformItems.frame: Qabil did not know [blank] with his brother’s dead body.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: When we report words after a past verb (admitted, did not know), a finished past action can move back to the past perfect: “he had killed”. Inside a sentence, a question word is followed by normal statement order: “what he should do”, not “what should he do”. “What to do” is a shorter way to say the same thing.

feedback.correct: Well done. You reported the admission and the uncertainty correctly.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: change “I” to “he” and move “killed” back in time. Item 2: after “what”, put the subject before “should”.

languageFocusExercises.title: From a Bad Choice to a Better Next Step
